_metadata.descripcion: Descriptores semanticos del analisis bibliometrico-semantico del corpus de movilidad urbana.
_metadata.agregacion: Para cada descriptor se calcula la similitud coseno con cada uno de los tres modelos y se utiliza el promedio de las tres similitudes.
_metadata.dos_planos: 'dimensions' son orientaciones tematicas y compiten entre si por argmax. 'empirical_axes' son modos de produccion empirica, se miden de forma transversal y NO entran en el argmax: un mismo documento puede puntuar alto en varios a la vez.
_metadata.ejes_empiricos: Los tres ejes se redactaron con fronteras mutuas. OBSERVACION_TERRENO registra sin preguntar; INTERACCION_ESTRUCTURADA pregunta con las respuestas ya categorizadas de antemano; INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL interactua con apertura al relato. La encuesta origen-destino pertenece al segundo: hay una persona delante, pero lo que puede decir esta fijado antes del encuentro.
_metadata.prueba_de_validacion_fijada_de_antemano: Los documentos que mencionan encuestas origen-destino o de hogares deben concentrarse en el decil superior de INTERACCION_ESTRUCTURADA y NO en el de OBSERVACION_TERRENO ni en el de INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL. Los documentos con metodos cualitativos deben concentrarse en INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL. Los de aforos y conteos, en OBSERVACION_TERRENO. Si la encuesta O-D sigue alta en OBSERVACION_TERRENO, el descriptor no quedo limpio.
_metadata.descriptores_retirados: PRESENCIA_CAMPO y CONTACTO_DIRECTO pasan a 'exploratory_descriptors'. El primero mezclaba observacion con encuesta -las encuestas O-D alcanzaban el 28,5 % del decil superior frente al 3,8 % de los trabajos etnograficos-; el segundo quedo asociado a INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL (r = 0,942 sobre 53.105) y no es una sintesis neutral. Se conservan solo para poder comparar con la corrida anterior.

relevance.URBAN_MOBILITY_TRANSPORT: Research in which the substantive object of study is the physical movement, travel, accessibility, or transportation of people or goods within an urban or metropolitan context. This includes urban public transport, buses, metro, tram and rail services; private vehicle travel and urban traffic; walking, cycling and active mobility; commuting, trips and travel; passenger movement; urban freight and city logistics; transport networks, services, infrastructure, planning and operations when these are examined as components of urban mobility or transportation. The defining criterion is that urban mobility or urban transport itself constitutes a central object of the research rather than merely an incidental application context.

dimensions.TECNICISTA: Urban mobility or transport approached as a system, network, infrastructure, or operation whose functioning, efficiency, performance, cost, design, prediction, control, or optimization constitutes the central research problem. This includes route and network optimization, traffic flow, congestion, scheduling and frequencies, capacity, level of service, reliability, and intelligent transportation systems; the economic evaluation of transport through operating costs, cost-benefit analysis, pricing, fares, tolls, demand modelling, generalized cost, and economic efficiency; and the instruments through which this knowledge is produced, namely mathematical and statistical modelling, econometric estimation, regression and discrete choice models, traffic and transport simulation, forecasting, algorithms, optimization procedures, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and the exploitation of large-scale digital datasets, sensor records, and big data sources.
dimensions.AMBIENTAL: Environmental impacts, externalities, or consequences of urban mobility or transport, substantively measured, modelled, or evaluated. This includes greenhouse gas and CO2 emissions, air pollution and air quality, traffic noise, energy consumption, fossil fuel use, climate change, carbon footprint, decarbonization, life-cycle assessment, environmental sustainability and sustainable mobility, and ecological impacts directly attributable to transport systems and mobility practices.
dimensions.SOCIAL_HUMANA: Urban mobility or transport examined in relation to people, social groups, and human experience -- combining the empirical description of social differences, inequalities, or lived mobility experiences among population groups with explicit ethical or normative reflection on the meaning, justice, dignity, care, responsibility, or human significance of mobility. This includes social exclusion, poverty, unequal accessibility, socio-spatial segregation, and differences in access to opportunities among groups defined by income, class, gender, age, disability, ethnicity, or other social positions, together with moral perception, virtue, care, hospitality, recognition, responsibility, alterity, and explicit reflection on justice, injustice, dignity, or the human meaning of movement and encounter.

empirical_axes.OBSERVACION_TERRENO: Empirical material generated by observing, counting or measuring what happens at a real-world site. This includes manual counts of vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists and passengers; turning-movement counts and vehicle classification counts; spot-speed, travel-time and delay measurements; headway, saturation-flow and queue-length observations; occupancy registers and boarding and alighting counts; on-site audits and walkability, safety or infrastructure inspections; instrumented, video-based or sensor-based recording at a site; and systematic direct observation of movement and behaviour at streets, intersections, stations, stops, platforms, corridors and transport facilities. The defining feature is that the empirical material consists of what the researcher registers on site.
empirical_axes.INTERACCION_ESTRUCTURADA: Empirical material generated by asking participants questions whose answers are recorded through categories, options, scales or variables defined in advance by the research design. This includes origin-destination surveys, household travel surveys, national and metropolitan travel surveys, intercept, roadside and on-board surveys, self-administered, postal, telephone, online and face-to-face questionnaires, structured interviews and structured travel or activity diaries, stated preference and revealed preference instruments, discrete choice experiments, rating items and Likert scales, and the measurement of satisfaction, acceptance, perceived quality, willingness to pay and behavioural intention, together with the treatment of the resulting answers as variables. The defining feature is that what a participant may answer is fixed by the instrument before the encounter takes place.
empirical_axes.INTERACCION_EXPERIENCIAL:
Empirical knowledge generated through direct interaction with people in order
to understand their situated mobility practices, experiences, perceptions,
interpretations, accounts or meanings. This includes ethnographic fieldwork
involving participants, participant observation, in-depth and semi-structured
interviews, qualitative interviews with participants or informants, focus
groups, oral histories, life-history interviews, go-along, ride-along and
walk-along methods, participant-kept diaries, photo-elicitation with
participants, participatory workshops, co-design, co-creation and
participatory action research.

exploratory_descriptors.PRESENCIA_CAMPO:
Empirical data generated through direct observation or measurement in
real-world mobility or transport settings. This includes manual traffic counts,
pedestrian counts, turning-movement counts, vehicle classification counts,
spot-speed measurements, travel-time and delay studies, queue-length
observations, parking occupancy surveys, roadside and intersection
observations, on-site audits, field inspections, direct observation of
pedestrian or vehicle movements, and field-based measurements conducted at
streets, intersections, stations, stops, corridors or transport facilities.
exploratory_descriptors.CONTACTO_DIRECTO:
Empirical knowledge generated through the researcher's direct presence in
real-world mobility or transport settings or through direct interaction with
people participating in those settings. This includes manual traffic and
pedestrian counts, turning-movement counts, vehicle classification counts,
speed and travel-time measurements, delay and queue observations, parking
surveys, roadside and intersection observations, on-site audits, field
inspections, direct observation at streets, stations, stops, corridors or
transport facilities, as well as ethnographic fieldwork, interviews, focus
groups, oral histories, go-along, ride-along and walk-along methods,
participant diaries, participatory workshops, co-design, co-creation and
participatory action research. The defining feature is that empirical material
is generated through direct presence in the mobility setting or direct
engagement with people involved in mobility.
